# Built-in function reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs` from src/stdlib (definitions and docs.ts). Do not edit by hand. -->

Every function can be called as `name(a, b)` or chained as `a:name(b)`, which passes `a` as the first argument.
Operators are functions too: `$a + $b` is `add($a, $b)`. *Pure* functions have no side effects and depend only on their arguments;
the optimizer may evaluate them at compile time. Optional parameters are in `[brackets]`.

## Operators

| Function | Operator | Precedence | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add(a, b)` | `+` | 3 | Adds numbers or concatenates strings (`+`). Example: `1 + 2 → 3` |
| `sub(a, b)` | `-` | 3 | Subtracts (`-`). Example: `5 - 2 → 3` |
| `mul(a, b)` | `*` | 3.1 | Multiplies (`*`). Example: `2 * 3 → 6` |
| `div(a, b)` | `/` | 3.1 | Divides (`/`). Example: `7 / 2 → 3.5` |
| `mod(a, b)` | `%` | 3.1 | Remainder (`%`). Example: `7 % 4 → 3` |
| `pow(a, b)` | `**` | 3.2, right | Exponentiation (`**`, right-associative). Example: `2 ** 3 → 8` |
| `neg(a)` | `-` (prefix) | 0 | Unary minus; applies to the whole chain that follows it. Example: `-$.x` |
| `eq(a, b)` | `==` | 2 | Loose equality (`==`). Example: `1 == '1' → true` |
| `eqq(a, b)` | `===` | 2 | Strict equality (`===`). Example: `1 === '1' → false` |
| `neq(a, b)` | `!=` | 2 | Loose inequality (`!=`). |
| `neqq(a, b)` | `!==` | 2 | Strict inequality (`!==`). |
| `gt(a, b)` | `>` | 2 | Greater than (`>`). |
| `gte(a, b)` | `>=` | 2 | Greater than or equal (`>=`). |
| `lt(a, b)` | `<` | 2 | Less than (`<`). |
| `lte(a, b)` | `<=` | 2 | Less than or equal (`<=`). |
| `or(a, b)` | `\|\|` | 1 | Short-circuit or (`\|\|`); returns the deciding operand, not a boolean. Example: `'x' \|\| 'y' → 'x'` |
| `and(a, b)` | `&&` | 1.1 | Short-circuit and (`&&`); returns the deciding operand, not a boolean. Example: `$.a && $.a.b` |
| `not(a)` | `!` (prefix) | 1.2 | Logical not (`!`); applies to the whole chain that follows it. Example: `!$.active` |
| `notNot(a)` | `!!` (prefix) | 1.2 | Converts to boolean (`!!`). Example: `!!$.name` |

## Conditional and errors

| Function | Pure | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ifElse(cond, thenReturn, elseReturn)` | no | Evaluates only the chosen branch. Also written `A if C else B`. Example: `ifElse($.age >= 18, 'adult', 'minor')` |
| `ifNull(val, valIfNull, [valIfNotNull])` | yes | `valIfNull` if the value is `null`; otherwise `valIfNotNull`, or the value itself when that is omitted. Example: `ifNull($.x, 0)` |
| `ifUndefined(val, valIfNull, [valIfNotNull])` | yes | Like `ifNull`, for `undefined`. |
| `ifNullOrUndefined(val, valIfNull, [valIfNotNull])` | yes | Like `ifNull`, for `null` or `undefined`. Example: `ifNullOrUndefined($.x, 'n/a')` |
| `notNull(value)` | yes | The value, or an error `Value cannot be null.` if it is `null` or `undefined`. Example: `$.id:notNull` |
| `throw(arg)` | no | Throws an error with the message (evaluated lazily). Example: `throw('missing id')` |
| `catch(value, [catchValue])` | no | The value, or `catchValue` (default `null`) if evaluating it throws. Both are evaluated lazily. Example: `$.a.b.c:catch('n/a')` |

## Collections

| Function | Pure | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `assign(...objects)` | yes | Merges the own properties of its arguments into a new object (later arguments win; `null` arguments are skipped). Example: `assign($.a, $.b)` |
| `map(arr, lambda)` | yes | Array of `lambda(item, index)` for each item. Example: `$.items:map($i => $i * 2)` |
| `sort(arr, [lambda])` | yes | Sorted copy; stable. With a key lambda the keys are computed once per item; without one, JavaScript's default (string) order. Example: `$.people:sort($p => $p.age)` |
| `reverse(arr)` | yes | Reversed copy. Example: `[1, 2, 3]:reverse → [3, 2, 1]` |
| `indexOf(arr, value)` | yes | Index of the first item equal (`===`) to the value, or -1; `undefined` if the first argument is not an array. |
| `findIndex(arr, lambda)` | yes | Index of the first item for which the lambda is truthy, or -1. Example: `$.items:findIndex($i => $i.id == 5)` |
| `filter(value, lambda)` | yes | Array: the items for which `lambda(item, index)` is truthy. Object: the entries for which `lambda(key, value)` is truthy. Example: `$.items:filter($i => $i.active)` |
| `reduce(arr, lambda, identity)` | yes | Folds the array with `lambda(accumulator, item, index)`, starting from `identity`. Example: `$.n:reduce(($a, $b) => $a + $b, 0)` |
| `find(arr, lambda)` | yes | The first item for which the lambda is truthy, or `undefined`. Example: `$.items:find($i => $i.id == 5)` |
| `slice(arr, startIndex, [stopIndex])` | yes | Copy of the items from `startIndex` up to (not including) `stopIndex`. Example: `[1, 2, 3, 4]:slice(1, 3) → [2, 3]` |
| `splice(arr, startIndex, deleteCount, ...addItems)` | yes | Copy with `deleteCount` items removed at `startIndex` and the extra arguments inserted there. Never changes the original. |
| `concat(a, ...other)` | yes | One array of the arguments: array arguments are spread, other values appended, `null` arguments skipped. Example: `concat($.a, $.b, 5)` |
| `min(arr, [lambda])` | yes | Smallest value (of the key lambda's results), ignoring `null`; `null` for an empty array. Example: `$.prices:min` |
| `findMin(arr, [lambda])` | yes | The item with the smallest key (the value itself without a lambda). Example: `$.items:findMin($i => $i.price)` |
| `max(arr, [lambda])` | yes | Largest value (of the key lambda's results), ignoring `null`; `null` for an empty array. Example: `$.prices:max` |
| `findMax(arr, [lambda])` | yes | The item with the largest key (the value itself without a lambda). Example: `$.items:findMax($i => $i.price)` |
| `avg(arr, [lambda])` | yes | Average of the numeric values (of the key lambda's results); `null` values are skipped, non-numbers throw, `null` when there are none. Example: `$.scores:avg` |
| `length(arr)` | yes | Number of items (or characters in a string). Example: `$.items:length` |
| `range(min, max, [incr])` | yes | Numbers from `min` up to (not including) `max`, stepping by `incr` (default 1). Example: `range(0, 5) → [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` |
| `item(arr, index)` | yes | The item at the index (a safe, hardened read). Example: `$.items:item(2)` |
| `first(arr)` | yes | The first item, or `undefined` for an empty or missing array. |
| `last(arr)` | yes | The last item, or `undefined` for an empty or missing array. |

## Strings

| Function | Pure | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `toString(val)` | yes | Converts to a string. Example: `(1.5 + 3):toString → '4.5'` |
| `substr(str, startIndex, length)` | yes | Substring from `startIndex` of `length` characters. Example: `'hello':substr(1, 3) → 'ell'` |
| `substring(str, startIndex, [stopIndex])` | yes | Substring from `startIndex` up to (not including) `stopIndex`. Example: `'hello':substring(1, 3) → 'el'` |
| `startsWith(str, test)` | yes | Whether the string starts with `test`. |
| `endsWith(str, test)` | yes | Whether the string ends with `test`. |
| `contains(str, test)` | yes | Whether the string contains `test`. |
| `split(str, separator)` | yes | Splits the string at every `separator`. Example: `'a,b':split(',') → ['a', 'b']` |
| `join(items, separator)` | yes | Joins the items with `separator`. Example: `['a', 'b']:join('-') → 'a-b'` |
| `toUpperCase(str)` | yes | Upper case. |
| `toLowerCase(str)` | yes | Lower case. |
| `toTitleCase(str)` | yes | Capitalizes each space-separated word. Example: `'hello world':toTitleCase → 'Hello World'` |
| `toSnakeCase(str)` | yes | Joins the space-separated words with `_`. Example: `'hello world':toSnakeCase → 'hello_world'` |
| `toCamelCase(str)` | yes | Camel case from words separated by spaces or punctuation, or by a change of case. Example: `'hello_big world':toCamelCase → 'helloBigWorld'` |
| `trim(str)` | yes | Removes leading and trailing whitespace. |
| `trimLeft(str)` | yes | Removes leading whitespace. |
| `trimRight(str)` | yes | Removes trailing whitespace. |
| `replace(val, orig, [repl])` | yes | Replaces every occurrence of `orig` with `repl` (nothing if omitted). Example: `'a-b-c':replace('-', '+') → 'a+b+c'` |

## Dates and times

| Function | Pure | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `now()` | no | The current date and time (a `Date`). Not pure. |
| `dateTime(val)` | yes | A `Date` from a string, a timestamp or another `Date`. Example: `dateTime('2020-01-02T03:04:05Z')` |
| `toISODateTime(val)` | yes | ISO 8601 UTC string (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`). Example: `toISODateTime('2020-01-02') → '2020-01-02T00:00:00.000Z'` |
| `toISOLocalDateTime(val, [offsetMinutes])` | yes | ISO 8601 string with a UTC offset. `offsetMinutes` follows `Date.getTimezoneOffset()` (minutes *west* of UTC, so -60 is `+01:00`); by default the host's offset at that date. Example: `toISOLocalDateTime($.t, 0)` |

## Math

Each is the JavaScript `Math` function of the same name, called with the same arguments, e.g. `math~floor($.x / 10)`.
`math~random` is the only impure one. Constants take no arguments: `math~E`, `math~LN10`, `math~LN2`, `math~LOG10E`, `math~LOG2E`, `math~PI`, `math~SQRT1_2`, `math~SQRT2`.

Functions: `math~abs`, `math~acos`, `math~acosh`, `math~asin`, `math~asinh`, `math~atan`, `math~atanh`, `math~atan2`, `math~ceil`, `math~cbrt`, `math~expm1`, `math~clz32`, `math~cos`, `math~cosh`, `math~exp`, `math~floor`, `math~fround`, `math~hypot`, `math~imul`, `math~log`, `math~log1p`, `math~log2`, `math~log10`, `math~max`, `math~min`, `math~pow`, `math~random`, `math~round`, `math~sign`, `math~sin`, `math~sinh`, `math~sqrt`, `math~tan`, `math~tanh`, `math~trunc`.

## Other

| Function | Pure | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `log(desc, val)` | no | Writes `desc` and the value to the console and returns the value. Not pure. Example: `log('total', $.total)` |
